practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum age required for a person to be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha under the Constitution of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 84(b) of the Constitution, the minimum age for contesting and becoming a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years. For the Rajya Sabha, it is 30 years. 21 years is the minimum age for contesting local body elections.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution are the qualifications for membership of Parliament laid down?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 84 of the Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament. Article 79 relates to the constitution of Parliament, Article 80 to the composition of the Council of States, and Article 102 to disqualifications for membership.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum age requirement to become a member of the Rajya Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 84(b) of the Constitution, a person must be not less than 30 years of age to be qualified to fill a seat in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

practiceQuestions.q: Who decides on any question relating to the disqualification of a member of Parliament under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law)?
opts: Chairman of Rajya Sabha or Speaker of Lok Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, the question of disqualification under anti-defection law is decided by the Chairman in the case of Rajya Sabha and the Speaker in the case of Lok Sabha (and not by the President).

practiceQuestions.q: Before taking his seat in Parliament, every member has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation. Who administers this oath to the members of Parliament?
opts: The President or some person appointed in that behalf by him
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 99 of the Constitution, every member of either House of Parliament shall, before taking his seat, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following acts enacted by Parliament prescribed additional disqualifications for membership of Parliament, such as prevention of corruption and electoral offenses?
opts: The Representation of the People Act, 1950
The Representation of the People Act, 1951
practiceQuestions.sol: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 contains provisions relating to disqualifications for membership of Parliament and state legislatures, including corrupt practices, electoral offenses, conviction for certain crimes, and failure to lodge account of election expenses.

practiceQuestions.q: If a member of Parliament is absent from all meetings of the House without the permission of the House for a period of how many days, can the House declare their seat vacant?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 101(4) of the Constitution, if for a period of 60 days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant. (In computing this period, no account is taken of any period during which the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days).

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 103, before deciding on any question of disqualification (other than under the Tenth Schedule), the President must obtain the opinion of which constitutional body?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 103 states that if any question arises whether a member of Parliament has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in Article 102(1), the question shall be referred to the President, whose decision shall be final. However, before giving any decision, the President must obtain the opinion of the Election Commission and act according to such opinion.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens if a person is elected to both Houses of Parliament? Under the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, how is the seat vacated?
opts: Both seats automatically become vacant immediately.
The person chooses which House to serve; otherwise, the Rajya Sabha seat becomes vacant.
The person must intimate within 10 days which House they wish to serve; failing which the Lok Sabha seat becomes vacant.
The person's seat in the Rajya Sabha becomes vacant if they fail to specify within 10 days, or as per rules prescribed.
The person specifies within 10 days which House to serve; if not, the Lok Sabha seat becomes vacant first, or specific statutory timelines apply.

Note: Under Section 68 of the RPA 1951, if a person is elected to both Houses, they must intimate within 10 days which house they want to serve. If they fail to do so, their seat in the Rajya Sabha becomes vacant. (Let's keep a simplified standard question style).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution penalizes a person for sitting and voting in Parliament when they know they are not qualified or are disqualified, making them liable to a penalty of Rs. 500 per day?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 104 of the Constitution provides for penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation under Article 99 or when not qualified or when disqualified. The penalty is Rs. 500 for each day they so sit or vote, recoverable as a debt due to the Union.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution of India prohibit a person from being a member of both Houses of Parliament simultaneously, and what is the constitutional mechanism to resolve it?
opts: To prevent concentration of legislative power and ensure distinct representation, resolved through statutory rules under RPA 1951 requiring vacation of one seat.
To prevent dual voting rights in Presidential elections.
To avoid quorum issues during joint sittings.
To enable the Prime Minister to exercise veto over bicameral decisions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Dual membership of both Houses violates the federal and bicameral ethos where Lok Sabha represents the people and Rajya Sabha represents states. Section 69 of RPA 1951 provides rules when a person is elected to both Houses, ensuring they cannot sit in both.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the principle of 'Office of Profit' under Article 102(1)(a) protect the independence of the legislature from the executive?
opts: It ensures that legislators do not accept lucrative executive appointments that could compromise their voting independence and create conflict of interest.
It bars all government employees from voting in general elections.
It prohibits ministers from being members of the Lok Sabha.
It gives the judiciary veto power over cabinet appointments.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 'Office of Profit' disqualification prevents the executive from influencing legislators by offering them paid government posts, thereby maintaining the separation of powers and legislative independence.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication if a person disqualified under the Tenth Schedule continues to sit and vote in Parliament?
opts: They are subject to penalties under Article 104 and their votes during that period can be invalidated or challenged in court post-Speaker's ruling.
The Supreme Court automatically dissolves the House.
They become eligible for cabinet rank automatically.
The President can suspend the Constitution under Article 356.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sitting and voting while disqualified attracts penalties under Article 104 (Rs. 500/day). Additionally, judicial review applies to Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule post-Kihoto Hollohan judgment.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of disqualification under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, what is the impact of a conviction with a sentence of two years or more on a sitting MP?
opts: Immediate disqualification from the date of conviction, subject to the protection of Supreme Court's Lily Thomas judgment removing the 3-month stay window.
Disqualification only after the Speaker gives explicit permission.
No disqualification unless the Election Commission holds a public referendum.
Automatic suspension for 30 days followed by presidential pardon.
practiceQuestions.sol: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA 1951, which allowed convicted MPs/MLAs a 3-month window to appeal. Now, conviction resulting in imprisonment for 2 years or more leads to immediate disqualification.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Tenth Schedule handle the disqualification of nominated members of Parliament if they join a political party?
opts: They can join any political party within 6 months of taking their seat without facing disqualification; joining after 6 months incurs disqualification.
They are permanently barred from joining any political party under any circumstance.
They can join a party immediately without any time restriction.
Nominated members are automatically treated as members of the ruling party.
practiceQuestions.sol: Paragraph 2(3) of the Tenth Schedule states that a nominated member of a House shall be disqualified if they join any political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which they take their seat.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are decisions regarding disqualifications under Article 103 (non-anti-defection) routed through the President on the advice of the Election Commission rather than decided by the House itself?
opts: To maintain political neutrality and insulate the process from partisan legislative majorities and parliamentary politics.
Because Parliament lacks legislative competence over its own members.
To give the executive absolute power to unseat opposition members at will.
To comply with international parliamentary conventions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Entrusting the decision to the President acting on the Election Commission's advice protects MPs from arbitrary removal by a hostile House majority, ensuring an objective, quasi-judicial inquiry by an independent constitutional body.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of Article 101 regarding simultaneous membership of Parliament and a State Legislature?
opts: If a person is elected to both Parliament and a State Legislature, their seat in Parliament becomes vacant unless they resign from the State Legislature within 14 days.
It allows dual representation as a bridge between central and state planning.
It mandates automatic forfeiture of both seats.
It requires prior permission from the Governor of the state.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 101(2) and RPA 1951 rules state that a person cannot be a member of both Parliament and a State Legislature. If elected to both, their seat in Parliament falls vacant if they do not resign from the State Legislature within the stipulated time.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Tenth Schedule impact the freedom of speech and vote of an individual MP within Parliament?
opts: It subordinates individual conscience and dissent to party whips on matters of voting, limiting intra-party dissent under threat of disqualification.
It completely abolishes the whip system in India.
It prevents MPs from speaking on any bill without party clearance.
It protects MPs from any form of disciplinary action by their political parties.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Anti-Defection law requires MPs to vote according to party directives or risk disqualification, which critics argue curtails independent legislative judgment and internal party democracy.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the rationale behind disqualifying a person under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 for failing to lodge an account of election expenses within the prescribed time?
opts: To enforce electoral transparency, curb the pernicious influence of black money, and maintain financial accountability in elections.
To generate government revenue through late fees and penalties.
To reduce paperwork for the Election Commission.
To ensure that only wealthy candidates can contest elections.
practiceQuestions.sol: Transparency in campaign financing is core to a clean democracy. Section 10A of the RPA 1951 provides for disqualification for failure to lodge election expense accounts, preventing unchecked financial corruption.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are certain constitutional offices, such as Ministers of the Union or States, explicitly exempted from the 'Office of Profit' disqualification under Article 102(2)?
opts: Because the parliamentary system is based on the fusion of executive and legislature, requiring ministers to be members of Parliament.
Because ministers do not draw any salary from the Consolidated Fund of India.
To allow the Prime Minister absolute control over judicial appointments.
To bypass the requirements of the Tenth Schedule entirely.
practiceQuestions.sol: In a parliamentary democracy, ministers are drawn from Parliament and are part of the executive, forming a harmonious fusion of powers. Article 102(2) explicitly protects Ministers from being disqualified under office of profit rules.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications for membership of Parliament:
1. A person contesting election to the Lok Sabha must make and subscribe to an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule before filing their nomination.
2. The Constitution fixes the maximum age limit for a person to remain a member of either House of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: Statement 1 is incorrect: The oath or affirmation under Article 99 is taken *after* being elected and before taking a seat in the House, not before filing nomination. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Constitution does not set any maximum age limit for members of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding disqualifications for membership of Parliament under Article 102:
1. A person is disqualified if they hold any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, without exception.
2. If a person is declared of unsound mind by a competent court, they stand disqualified from being a member of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Parliament has declared certain offices (like Ministers) as exempt from office of profit disqualification via the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act. Statement 2 is correct: Article 102(1)(b) states that a person is disqualified if they stand so declared by a competent court.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the decision on disqualification of members of Parliament:
1. All disqualification disputes under Article 102(1) are decided by the President of India on the opinion of the Election Commission.
2. Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) is decided by the Speaker or Chairman of the respective House, and their decision is immune from judicial review.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 103 mandates President's decision based on Election Commission's opinion for Article 102(1) disqualifications. Statement 2 is incorrect because in Kihoto Hollohan (1992), the Supreme Court held that the Speaker's decision under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding vacation of seats in Parliament:
1. If a member of Parliament is elected to the State Legislature, their seat in Parliament does not become vacant immediately if they apply for extension.
2. If a seat in Parliament is declared vacant due to absence without permission for 60 days, the decision cannot be challenged in court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Under Article 101(2), if a person is elected to both Parliament and a State Legislature, their seat in Parliament falls vacant unless they resign from the State Legislature within the stipulated period (no extension provision). Statement 2 is incorrect: House proceedings and decisions can be judicially reviewed if there is illegality or violation of constitutional mandates.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provisions on candidate qualifications:
1. A person contesting an election to the Rajya Sabha from a particular state must be an elector in that same state.
2. In 2003, Parliament removed the requirement of being a registered voter in the specific state for election to the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are tricky. Originally, Rajya Sabha candidates had to be electors in the state they represented. In 2003, the requirement was amended, but the requirement to be an elector in *some* constituency in India was retained, while domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha was removed (i.e., you don't need to be from that state, but you must be an elector in India). Wait, let's verify precisely: Statement 1 says 'must be an elector in that same state' - this was the rule amended in 2003 (domicile requirement removed). Statement 2 says 'removed the requirement of being a registered voter in the specific state' - this is correct. Let's re-evaluate options.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the disqualification of legislators under the Tenth Schedule:
1. If a member voluntarily gives up membership of their political party, they become liable for disqualification.
2. If a member votes against the directives of their political party during a confidence motion without obtaining prior permission or condonation within 15 days, they face disqualification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: Statement 1 is correct: Voluntary resignation from a party attracts disqualification under Paragraph 2(1)(a). Statement 2 is incorrect because the condonation period provided under the Tenth Schedule for unauthorized voting is 15 days, but let's check the exact rule: voting or abstaining without permission, if condoned within 15 days, prevents disqualification. Wait, the 15-day condonation rule for voting/abstention without whip permission makes statement 2 correct? Let's check: Paragraph 2(1)(b) states that if a member votes or abstains contrary to party whip, and the party condones it within 15 days, they are saved. Thus, statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding dual membership and vacation of seats:
1. A person cannot be a member of both Parliament and a State Legislature simultaneously.
2. If a person is elected to two seats in the Lok Sabha in a general election, both seats must be vacated immediately and a fresh bye-election held for both.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct under Article 101(2). Statement 2 is incorrect: if a person is elected to two seats in Lok Sabha, they must resign from one within the specified period; only one seat becomes vacant, not both automatically without option.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding disqualifications under Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. Disqualification is triggered upon conviction for certain specified offenses, including untouchability, dowry, and human trafficking.
2. A person convicted of any offense and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than two years is disqualified from the date of conviction and remains disqualified for an additional period of six years after release.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 8 of RPA 1951 lists specific offenses (untouchability, dowry, FEMA violations, corruption, etc.) leading to disqualification upon conviction, and imprisonment for 2 years or more disqualifies a person for the jail term plus 6 years post-release.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the vacation of seats due to disqualification and resignation:
1. A member of the Lok Sabha can resign their seat by writing to the President of India.
2. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha can reject a member's resignation if it appears to him from information or personal knowledge that the resignation is not voluntary or genuine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Lok Sabha members address their resignation to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, not the President. Statement 2 is correct: Under Articles 101(3)(b) (as amended by the 33rd Constitutional Amendment Act), the Speaker or Chairman can conduct an inquiry and refuse to accept a resignation if it is not voluntary or genuine.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding disqualification on grounds of defection under the Tenth Schedule:
1. A legislature party can merge with another party if not less than two-thirds of its members agree to the merger without attracting disqualification.
2. If a speaker or chairman resigns from their political party upon election to the presiding office and does not rejoin it later, they are not disqualified under the anti-defection law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule permits a merger if 2/3rd of the party legislators agree. Paragraph 5 exempts the Speaker or Chairman from disqualification if they voluntarily give up party membership upon election and do not rejoin, or rejoin later.
